incident_report.incident: Sent for sampling post-race.
Sent for sampling post-race.

Jumped awkwardly.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Near the winning post on the first occasion was steadied away from the heels of PERFECT PEACH.  Passing the 200 Meres was shifted out away from SMILING EMPEROR to obtain clear running.

Passing the winning post on the first occasion was steadied when placed in restricted room to the inside of BLING BLING GENIUS which was racing tight to the inside of RUN RUN TIMING (R Kingscote) which was taking up a forward position.  R Kingscote was reprimanded for failing to leave sufficient racing room for runners to his inside.
Slow to begin.  Approaching the winning post on the first occasion was bumped on the hindquarters by PERFECT PEACH.
From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.

Had its left hind plate refitted in the saddling stalls, was examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race.  Crowded for room approaching the winning post on the first occasion.  For a short distance after passing the 300 Metres was held up for clear running.

A short distance after the start was bumped by MEEPMEEP which shifted in.  H Bentley explained that due to the fast tempo in the early and middle stages he elected to leave the running line to a three wide position near the 700 Metres to improve as he felt that the field would come back to him given the fast tempo.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

B Avdulla pleaded guilty to a careless riding charge for causing interference approaching the winning post on the first occasion (see PERFECT PEACH).  Soon after the start shifted in before being straightened by its rider, however, in doing so bumped STRONGEST BOY.

B Avdulla (MEEPMEEP) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that approaching the winning post on the first occasion he permitted his mount to shift in when insufficiently clear of CARRYON SMILING, resulting in that horse being crowded in onto PERFECT PEACH which resulted in that horse being checked and making contact with the hindquarters of SMILING EMPEROR.  B Avdulla was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Wednesday, 4 March 2026 at Happy Valley.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his excellent race riding record.  K Teetan reported that after his mount received interference approaching the winning post on the first occasion it failed to travel at any stage after that.

Trainer F C Lor advised that the horse would be ridden in a forward position tonight.  H T Mo stated that after taking up a forward position, his mount was not able to handle the quick tempo of tonight’s race and failed to run out the 1650 Metres at its first attempt.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Z Purton could offer no explanation for his mount’s disappointing performance and added that BLING BLING GENIUS was under pressure 600 Metres from the winning post.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of BLING BLING GENIUS was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, BLING BLING GENIUS will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Over-raced in the middle stages.  Passing the 400 Metres raced awkwardly close to the heels of BRILLIANT FIRE and on the Home Turn was steadied and shifted in when disappointed for clear running between BRILLIANT FIRE and EXCEED THE WISH (L Hewitson) which shifted out.  In assessing the incident the Stewards were satisfied that the racing manners of TAIHANG SCENERY was the main contributor to the incident, however, L Hewitson was advised to exercise more care when shifting ground.  Passing the 300 Metres lay in and bumped the hindquarters of MODEST GENTLEMAN. .  Near the 200 Metres was disappointed for a run between EXCEED THE WISH and MODEST GENTLEMAN before then shifting back in to continue into clear running.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Bumped shortly after the start.  Passing the 300 Metres was bumped on the hindquarters by TAIHANG SCENERY which shifted in.
Sent for sampling post-race.

Fractious in the barriers and broke through prior to the start, however, was quickly restrained, examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race.  Jumped awkwardly.  Lay in in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. <12/2/2026 Additional Veterinary Report> After the race, WAVE GARDEN was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time there were no significant findings. WAVE GARDEN was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer K H Ting this morning. He said at this time he noted the horse to be lame in its left front leg. Before being allowed to race again, WAVE GARDEN will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

ABSOLUTE AWAKENED, which was standing awkwardly in the barriers, was removed and subsequently took its place back in the field.  Bumped on jumping by CALIFORNIA BANNER which shifted out.  Trainer F C Lor advised the instructions were to have the horse ridden in a midfield position.  It was noted that in the early stages ABSOLUTE AWAKENED was caught wide and had to be eased further back in the field to obtain cover in the running line.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Near the 300 Metres got unbalanced after being bumped by HARMONY GALAXY which shifted out.  K C Leung reported that his mount failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race revealed that the horse was displaying an irregular heart rhythm and an endoscopic examination also showed a substantial amount of blood in its trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, PRESTIGE RICKY will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

M Guyon reported that in the early stages he was caught wide and therefore elected to press on and take up a forward position to trail the leader.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

When questioned H Bentley explained that over the concluding stages his mount did not feel comfortable in its action and as he was concerned with the horse’s welfare he elected not to ride it out over the concluding stages.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of mucus in the horse’s trachea.  Given the manner in which the horse weakened over the concluding stages, the Stewards ruled that FLYING FORTRESS will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination before being allowed to race again.

Trainer C Fownes advised that the instructions were to ride the horse back in the field from a wide barrier with the amount of noted speed drawn inside.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Near the 700 Metres was checked and shifted out abruptly to avoid LUCKY EIGHT which had gone amiss.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Passing the 600 Metres got unbalanced when racing tight between PERFECT GENERAL and SPIRIT OF PEACE and subsequently lost ground when negotiating the 600 Metre turn.

After the 900 Metres went amiss and was retired out of the event.  When questioned B Avdulla explained that when his mount was negotiating the turn near the 900 Metres it changed legs and put in an awkward stride.  He said from that point the horse did not feel right in its action and therefore he was left with no option but to retire the horse out of the race.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be lame in its right hind leg.  Before being allowed to race again, LUCKY EIGHT will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination which must include additional diagnostic assessments.
